items.title: Sacked Ukraine defence minister urges path to elections
items.summary: KYIV: Ukraine's popular ex-defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sacked last month, on Tuesday called for a move towards elections that have been put off because of the Russian invasion. Ukraine imposed martial law when Russian forces swept over the border in February 2022, and military rule prohibits holding elections. Fedorov said Ukraine must find a "legal, safe, and realistic mechanism that will allow Ukraine to restore a full democratic process even amidst a prolonged war."

items.title: Kelantan police vow firm action against ‘tonto’ used to block enforcement in human‑smuggling cases
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 19 — Police will take firm action against human-smuggling syndicates using ‘tonto’ to obstruct enforcement vehicles, following a recent incident in which two General Operations Force (GOF) personnel were hit while carrying out their duties. Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the incident showed that the syndicates were becoming increasingly bold, stressing that such actions would not be tolerated. Mohd Yusoff said police had also detected human-smuggling activities using sea routes and rivers along the Kelantan coast, adding that enforcement agencies would remain vigilant against such operations.

items.title: Palestinian-American hoists US flag on home besieged by settlers
items.summary: QUSRA: A Palestinian-American has raised the US flag on his home besieged by Israeli settlers, as the United States renewed criticism of the siege that has generated condemnation around the world. "It's my message to all Americans in the United States to see what's going on here in the West Bank, how the settlers put us under siege trying to take my own house in the West Bank," Abu Ridi told AFP reporters inside his home. Under US pressure, the Israeli military said last week it had given orders to remove the settlers.

items.title: Govt must consider cost of living in minimum wage review, says UNI-MLC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's ongoing review of the Minimum Wages Order 2024 must consider the rising cost of living to ensure workers' incomes remain sufficient to support a decent standard of living. UNI Malaysian Labour Centre (UNI-MLC) president Datuk Mohamed Shafie BP Mammal said fluctuations in the cost of food, housing, transportation, and education directly affected workers' purchasing power, particularly for lower-income groups. He said the government's ongoing review of the Minimum Wages Order 2024 was important to determine whether the current rate remained relevant to workers' needs and prevailing economic conditions.

items.title: MB: Pahang reports end of recorded hardcore poverty, with 2,913 households lifted and overall poverty down 30pc
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 19 — Pahang’s hardcore poverty was brought to an end on Feb 19, with all 2,913 heads of household recorded in the Jan 15, 2026 figure removed from the status, said Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail. He said the state had also recorded a 30 per cent reduction in poverty, with 4,263 of the 14,210 heads of household classified as poor on June 5 subsequently removed from the category. Wan Rosdy said key factors behind the achievement included targeted assistance, initiatives and interventions provided by the state and federal governments and relevant agencies, as well as changes in household income and household size.

items.title: Immigration Dept opens internal probe after fatal KL crash that killed three
items.summary: In a statement posted on Facebook, Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would give its full cooperation to the police in determining the cause of the accident. Zakaria said the department would also conduct an internal investigation into compliance with standard operating procedures and safety aspects involving the operation of department vehicles to ensure the matter was thoroughly examined. Zakaria said the department viewed the incident seriously and would take appropriate action based on the findings of the police investigation and its internal probe.

items.title: Two parole inmates among trio jailed 8 months for trespass
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Two inmates under the Parole Release Programme were among three men sentenced to eight months in jail for trespassing into a house last week. Magistrate Aini Adilah Muhammad Faizal handed down the sentence to Zainudin Chik Ani, 46, Azizan Osman, 46, and Mohammad Asyraaf Zuhairi Adam Rizalee, 33, after they pleaded guilty. Zainudin and Azizan are serving sentences under the programme and were due for full release on Sept 11.

items.title: Temasek-backed Shiprocket jumps 35pct in debut trade after US$170mil India IPO
items.summary: BENGALURU: Temasek-backed e-commerce logistics services firm Shiprocket jumped 35.1 per cent in debut trade on Wednesday, after robust investor response to its US$170 million initial public offering last week. Its shares listed at 131 rupees on the National Stock Exchange of India, compared with an issue price of 97 rupees per share. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Make it rain: Indonesia chases clouds to stem El Nino fires
items.summary: INDONESIA'S Borneo, home to pristine rainforest and protected species, is burning. Indonesia believes cloud seeding can help it tackle a wildfire season that experts say is on track to be among the worst in years, driven by a strong El Nino. Indonesia's government says over 100,000 hectares burned in the first half of the year.

items.title: [UPDATED] Family was in designated safe zone when hit by Immigration truck
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The family of four struck by an Immigration Department truck in a fatal accident at the Jalan Sultan Ismail traffic light intersection early today had been standing in a safe area when they were hit. "Based on our investigation and observations of the CCTV footage of the incident, the family was in a safe area to cross the road when they were struck by the Immigration Department truck. CCTV footage showed the family of four standing at the road divider at the Jalan Sultan Ismail traffic light intersection, opposite Maju Junction, at 1am.

items.title: EP Manufacturing unveils RM9.5mil chassis component plant in Tanjung Malim
items.summary: The facility, operated by its joint venture Peps Sanly JV Sdn Bhd (Peps Sanly JV) with China-based automotive component maker Sanly Auto Parts Co Ltd (Sanly China), will produce critical components for selected Proton Holdings Bhd (Proton) models. Also present were EPMB executive chairman Hamidon Abdullah and Sanly China and Peps Sanly JV vice-president and director Ji Xiantao. Hamidon said the facility marked the continuation of EPMB's strategic partnership with Sanly China, following the joint venture's formal establishment in February 2025.

items.title: Immigration truck crash: Family were on KL holiday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The three family members killed in a crash involving an Immigration Department truck along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today are believed to have been in the capital for a holiday. It was reported that three family members, including a 12-year-old girl, were killed after an Immigration Department truck allegedly ran a red light , struck a car, and ploughed into pedestrians along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today. The Immigration truck, driven by a 43-year-old man, was travelling from the Kuala Lumpur Immigration office to Chow Kit to pick up detainees following an operation against undocumented migrants.

items.title: #NSTViral: Four flee after cable theft attempt in Bandar Dato Onn [WATCH]
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Four men fled in a car after they were believed to have been caught attempting to steal cables in Bandar Dato Onn here yesterday. Johor Baru (South) police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei confirmed the incident and said the auxiliary policeman lodged a report at 4.58pm the same day. @maszlee Kejadian curi kabel di Perjiranan 6/2, rumah contog Bandar Dato' Onn, JB PDRM sedang mengejar dan melakukan operasi untuk menjejaki pencuri.

items.title: More workplace subsidies, tax incentives needed to support breastfeeding mothers, says Yeo Bee Yin
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — The government should provide more subsidies and tax incentives to companies to set up breastfeeding rooms and childcare facilities in the workplace. “This includes breastfeeding rooms or multipurpose rooms where mothers can pump their milk, as well as childcare facilities in the workplace,” she said during a panel discussion titled ‘Realities of Breastfeeding’, held in conjunction with Toshiba Lifestyle Malaysia’s ‘World Breastfeeding Month 2026: Empowering Every Mother’s Journey’ event here yesterday. “Every child is different.

items.title: Child sex assault at Singapore mosque triggers review of safeguards
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Singapore's acting Minister-in-Charge of Muslim Affairs has ordered a review of mosque safeguards after an unaccredited religious influencer was jailed for sexually abusing five victims, including two young brothers. Zaqy Mohamad said the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) was directed to examine safety protocols at mosques after one of the offences occurred inside a mosque toilet. He described the case as deeply troubling, given that several offences took place at a mosque where religious guidance and community interactions occurred.

items.title: Johor Amanah sets up committee to monitor Rohingya issues
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Johor Amanah will set up a special committee to monitor issues involving the Rohingya refugee community amid concerns over public order, law compliance and tensions with local residents. Johor Amanah chairman Aminolhuda Hassan said the committee would gather complaints and information from residents before referring matters requiring action to the relevant authorities. Aminolhuda said the committee would also urge the state and federal governments to strengthen the management of refugee settlements, documentation, economic activities and compliance with the law.

items.title: [UPDATED] Immigration Dept to conduct internal probe into fatal Jalan Sultan Ismail crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department will conduct an internal investigation into compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) and safety measures following a fatal accident involving one of its vehicles along Jalan Sultan Ismail early today. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the review would focus on procedures and safety aspects governing departmental vehicles. He said the department viewed the incident seriously and would take appropriate action based on the findings of the police investigation and its internal probe.

items.title: Investment firm director previously charged with CBT now faces RM13.4m money‑laundering counts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — An investment company director, previously charged with criminal breach of trust, was brought before the Sessions Court here again today to face 10 charges of receiving RM13.4 million in proceeds from unlawful activities. Datuk Norliza Tajudin, 54, pleaded not guilty after all the charges were read out individually before Judge Suzana Hussin. “The prosecution also applies for this case to be tried jointly with the previous case (criminal breach of trust) in this court,” she said.

items.title: KL police destroy RM15.4m worth of drugs seized since 2007
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur police are disposing of more than RM15.4 million worth of drugs seized in cases dating back to 2007, following the completion of court proceedings. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the disposal involved 5,022 drug exhibits from 4,884 investigation papers opened between 2007 and 2025. "The drugs could have been abused by 382,739 users," he said at a drug exhibit disposal event here today.

items.title: Nilai private university CFO accused of RM6.56m CBT linked to IRB duty payments
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 19 — A chief financial officer (CFO) of a private university in Nilai pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to allegedly committing criminal breach of trust involving RM6.56 million in company funds between September 2025 and April this year. Noraini Aripin, 55, entered the plea after the charge was read out to her before Judge Datin M. Kunasundary Marimuthu. Deputy Public Prosecutor Syairah Aqilah Khalil sought bail of RM100,000 with two sureties, with the accused also required to surrender her passport to the court and report to the Negeri Sembilan Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office each month.

items.title: Singapore: No construction waste exported for disposal in Johor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Singapore does not allow construction and demolition (C&D) waste to be exported for disposal, its National Environment Agency (NEA) says following reports of such waste being dumped illegally in Pontian, Johor. NEA said it had contacted the Johor Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) to seek more information on C&D waste reportedly originating from Singapore. NEA said it had also issued an advisory to licensed general waste disposal facilities handling C&D waste in Singapore, reminding them of the relevant requirements.

items.title: Malaysia still exposed to oil price swings despite LNG strength – Kenanga Research
items.summary: However, Malaysia's fiscal position remains exposed to refined product prices through subsidies, while its trade position shows a crude oil deficit but a liquefied natural gas (LNG) surplus. In 2025, Malaysia ran a RM30.4 billion deficit in crude and condensate and only a RM3.2 billion surplus in refined products, resulting in a combined petroleum deficit of RM27.2 billion. "The overall oil and gas surplus of RM18.2 billion exists because of a RM45.4 billion LNG surplus," the bank said in a research note today.

items.title: F1 Malaysia return marred by ticket scalping, booking woes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The return of Formula One to Malaysia has sparked excitement and frustration among fans, with complaints of ticket scalping, long virtual queues and problems with official ticketing platforms. Other users reported being quoted RM350 and RM500, while some urged fans to avoid resellers offering Madani tickets for RM600. International fans also reported paying hefty markups after struggling to secure tickets through official channels.

items.title: Trump pauses 50pct tariffs on Canadian goods for three days
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump paused the planned rollout of new tariffs on Canadian goods late Tuesday, after negotiations between both countries that went down to the wire. The temporary reprieve from the 50-per cent duties would last three days, the US leader said in a social media post. Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

items.title: Norliza charged again, this time over RM13.4mil in unlawful proceeds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An investment company director, who was previously charged with criminal breach of trust, was brought before the Sessions Court here again today to face 10 charges of receiving RM13.4 million in proceeds from unlawful activities. Datuk Norliza Tajudin, 54, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out individually before Judge Suzana Hussin. Norliza was charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act.

items.title: Police send special team to Islamabad over Malaysians held in scam raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have dispatched a special team to Islamabad, Pakistan, to investigate reports regarding the detention of several Malaysians suspected of involvement in an online scam syndicate. Khalid said police were actively tracing the network of individuals involved in these activities with the cooperation of Pakistani authorities. Khalid revealed that current trends show online scam activities increasingly involve foreign nationals, particularly those from China.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Red light means stop': Road safety group warns official duties are no excuse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Government vehicle drivers must not treat official duties as a licence to disregard road traffic laws, the Road Safety Expert Association (PPKJR) said following a reported incident involving an Immigration Department vehicle that allegedly ran a red light and resulted in the deaths of 3 people . Its founder and road safety and motorsport advisor Jamil Manan Supri said running a red light was not a minor traffic offence and could result in sudden and fatal collisions with road users travelling lawfully. "When the traffic light is red, drivers must stop.

items.title: Malaysia's 4pct-5pct growth forecast now looks conservative, says economist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government's full-year growth forecast of between 4.0 and 5.0 per cent is now seen as conservative after the economy outperformed expectations in the first half of the year, an economist said. Dr Geoffrey Williams said Malaysia had shown resilience and was not suffering from an economic downturn despite the geopolitical crisis, mainly due to government policies. Malaysia's economy expanded 5.7 per cent in the first half of the year, driven by growth of 5.4 per cent in the first quarter and 6.0 per cent in the second quarter.

items.title: Former UBB Investment Bank CEO pleads not guilty to RM139.8m cheating charge
items.summary: Razlan Raghazli, 43, the former CEO of UBB Investment Bank Limited, entered the plea after the charge was read out to him before Judge Azura Alwi. He was charged with cheating the Managing Director and CEO of UBB Amanah Berhad, Aida Aizura Othman, 52, by deceiving her into believing that the payment schedule contained in a UBB Investment Bank Limited letter was in accordance with legal advice. However, the accused allegedly knew that the payment schedule in question actually contradicted the advice provided by the law firm.

items.title: Nilai university CFO claims trial over RM6.56mil CBT
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The chief financial officer (CFO) of a private university in Nilai pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of criminal breach of trust involving RM6.56 million in company funds between September last year and April this year. Noraini Aripin, 55, entered the plea after the charge was read before Judge Datin M. Kunasundary Marimuthu. The offence allegedly took place at the university's office between September 2025 and April 2026.

items.title: Chin Hin, UCSI team up on Melaka education hub
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Chin Hin Group Property Bhd (CHGP) is partnering UCSI Group to establish an integrated education hub that will anchor its 7.81-hectare waterfront masterplan within the Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone. The development will combine education, residential, lifestyle, commercial and future healthcare components, with the education hub positioned as a key catalyst for population growth, talent attraction and economic activity. UCSI will manage the school's education and operations, while CHGP will oversee the campus development.

items.title: MSC shares down 2.06pct in early trade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Smelting Corporation Bhd's (MSC) share price fell 2.06 per cent in early trading on Wednesday, following the announcement of a temporary suspension of its mining operations yesterday. The company said the Perak Department of Minerals and Geosciences (JMG Perak) directed its 80 per cent-owned subsidiary, Rahman Hydraulic Tin Sdn Bhd (RHT), to suspend mining operations temporarily. In a Bursa Malaysia filing, MSC said the directive, effective Aug 12, 2026, follows a site inspection conducted by JMG Perak at RHT's tin mine in Klian Intan, after about 60 millimetres of rainfall was recorded within one hour on Aug 3, 2026.

items.title: Police: Chinese national detained after allegedly disrupting passengers at KLIA, later admitted to psychiatric ward
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — A 27-year-old Chinese national who allegedly behaved aggressively towards passengers at Kuala Lumpur International Airport’s Terminal 1 building is believed to be mentally unwell and has been detained for further investigation, police said today. KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said authorities were alerted to the incident involving the woman at about 1.19pm on August 18, after she allegedly began shouting and disturbing passengers in the terminal's departure hall by running, singing and dancing. "Her partner later told police that she had forgotten to take her prescribed medication," he said.

items.title: ‘There may still be another way’: Sanusi signals Kedah will explore legal room to maintain zero-gambling stance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Kedah government will examine whether it has any legal avenues left to pursue its zero-gambling policy after the Federal Court rejected its bid to appeal a ruling over gambling licences, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor has said. That could amount to contempt of court. Asked whether the state government would issue new licences for gambling premises, Sanusi said no decision had been made.

items.title: Dollar drifts near multi-month lows as Treasury yields ease; Fed minutes awaited
items.summary: HONG KONG: The US dollar drifted near multi-month lows against major peers on Wednesday as Treasury yields eased from recent highs, with investors awaiting minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting for clues on the path of interest rates. Sterling was little changed at US$1.3533, holding near a three-month high ahead of British inflation data due later on Wednesday, which is widely expected to show persistent price pressure. The dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major peers, was down marginally at 99.65.

items.title: [UPDATED] Former investment bank CEO charged with RM139.8mil fraud
items.summary: Razlan Raghazli, 43, the former CEO of UBB Investment Bank Limited, entered the plea after the charge was read out before judge Azura Alwi. He was charged with deceiving UBB Amanah Bhd managing director and CEO Aida Aizura Othman, 52, into believing that a payment schedule in a UBB Investment Bank Limited letter complied with legal advice. However, the accused allegedly knew that the payment schedule contradicted the law firm's advice.

items.title: Equal isn't fair: Bangi MP calls for voter-based funding model
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Constituency allocations for members of parliament should take into account not only equal access but also the number of voters and circumstances of each constituency, said Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan. Syahredzan said Bangi had more than 300,000 registered voters as of 2022, a figure he believed had increased over the past few years. He said the constituency had roughly three times the national average number of registered voters.

items.title: TH depositors: Truth must not be hidden after RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tabung Haji (TH) depositors have described the disclosure of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report as an important and courageous step towards restoring the institution's integrity, governance and public confidence. Bank executive Anis Atifah Che Rawi, 39, a TH depositor since she was 25, welcomed the disclosure, saying it would allow depositors to understand the situation and ensure issues were addressed fairly and transparently. As a TH depositor, I hope this issue can be addressed transparently and fairly so that public confidence in TH remains intact," she told Bernama.

items.title: Education Ministry builds 2,102 classrooms for 2027 Year One intake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is implementing 681 projects nationwide to build 2,102 additional classrooms to accommodate increased Year One enrolment for the 2027 academic session. The ministry said RM668 million had been allocated for 524 projects in Peninsular Malaysia and Labuan, involving 1,780 classrooms — 1,255 mainstream and 525 Integrated Special Education Programme (PPKI) classrooms. In Sarawak, 84 projects costing RM81.5 million are underway to build 210 classrooms, while 73 projects costing RM58 million are being implemented in Sabah to build 112 classrooms.

items.title: Kelana Jaya LRT services back to normal after Putra Heights safety system fault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said the Kelana Jaya LRT Line resumed normal operations at 9.19am today after inspection and recovery works at Putra Heights station were completed. The public transport operator said the earlier disruption was caused by a fault involving the station’s safety detection system. Rapid KL said its technical team would continue monitoring the system and train movements to ensure services along the Kelana Jaya Line run smoothly.

items.title: Delays on Kelana Jaya LRT Line after suspected power supply fault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Rapid KL said today that services on the Kelana Jaya LRT Line are experiencing delays due to a suspected fault involving a power supply component at Putra Heights station. It said this would also slow train movements at nearby stations and result in longer waiting times for passengers on platforms. Passengers were advised to check Rapid KL’s social media channels or the MyRapid PULSE journey-planning app for the latest updates on Kelana Jaya Line services.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution hits out at recycled false claims of Home Ministry granting citizenship en masse to foreigners
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has denied claims that the Home Ministry (KDN) granted citizenship en masse to foreign nationals and that 1.2 million Chinese nationals had remained in Malaysia. Saifuddin Nasution said the matter had already been explained officially, with the facts documented in earlier statements and media reports. “Use social media responsibly.

items.title: Housing Ministry to nominate award-winning cleaning workers for state honours
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 19 — The Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) plans to nominate recipients of the 2026 Cleaning Workers Award for state honours in recognition of their service and sacrifices in keeping public spaces clean. “I have discussed this with Datuk Wira, and this year’s national cleaning workers award recipients will be listed and nominated to the respective state palaces to receive honours from the respective state rulers,” he said in his speech at the 2026 Cleaning Workers Appreciation Day here yesterday. He said the country’s solid waste management and public cleaning sector was currently supported by 26,889 workers employed by concessionaires.

items.title: PM Anwar orders immediate Immigration probe into fatal Maju Junction crash, vows no compromise if wrongdoing found
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered the Immigration Department to immediately conduct a thorough investigation into a crash involving one of its trucks that killed three members of a family at Maju Junction here early today. According to preliminary police investigations, the crash occurred at about 1am when an Immigration Department Isuzu “Black Maria” truck entered the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection against a red light with its beacon lights and siren activated. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the truck collided with a Proton Saga travelling through a green light before skidding into four pedestrians from the same family and an Inokom Matrix.

items.title: Crash with Immigration Dept truck at KL’s Maju Junction kills three family members
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Three members of a family were killed while another was injured after being hit by a Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM) truck at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection on Jalan Sultan Ismail here early today. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the accident occurred at about 1am when the unladen Isuzu ‘Black Maria’ truck was travelling from the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office towards Chow Kit for an operation targeting illegal immigrants. He said preliminary investigations found that the truck, driven by a 43-year-old local man, entered the intersection against a red light with its beacon lights and siren activated.

items.title: Housing minister urges waste separation to be taught young as Malaysia studies Japan’s recycling model
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Malaysia is looking to Japan’s waste separation and recycling practices as it seeks to make environmentally responsible habits part of everyday life and accelerate the country’s transition towards a circular economy. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said Japan’s experience in efficient waste management, particularly its practice of separating waste at source, could provide valuable lessons for Malaysia. In Japan, separating waste at source has become part of everyday life.

items.title: ‘I only wanted to save’: Kajang retiree wins RM1m Bank Rakyat lucky draw
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — A 68-year-old retiree never thought that his decision to save through Bank Rakyat’s Rizq Plus Investment-i Account would bring him such good fortune when he emerged as the winner of the Millionaire Draw, taking home a RM1 million prize. Meanwhile, Bank Rakyat chairman Datuk Mohd Irwan Mohd Mubarak said that Aziz is the fifth millionaire since the Rizq Plus Investment-i account was introduced in 2022. The Rizq Plus Investment-i account currently has over 250,000 customers, with total investments exceeding RM1 billion.

items.title: Govt must not to replace UUCA with another ‘oppressive’ law, says deputy education minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The new legal framework to be introduced following the repeal of the Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA) 1971 must strengthen university autonomy and academic freedom and avoid repeating the shortcomings of the repealed Act, said Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli Abd Halim. He said the new framework should bring reforms in various aspects, including ensuring more meaningful student participation in the governance of higher education institutions. Adam Adli said the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) has referred to various historical records, legal interpretations and fundamental recommendations such as the One Higher Education Act outlined in the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint to ensure that the new framework was built on clear principles.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Over 90pc chance of ‘Super El Nino’ by year-end, could rival 1997–1998 extreme
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 19 — The likelihood of El Nino, which typically brings hotter and drier conditions, reaching the ‘very strong’ or ‘Super El Nino’ category between October and December has risen to more than 90 per cent, according to Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip. Mohd Hisham said current global climate patterns indicated that the 2026-2027 El Nino could rank among the most extreme events ever recorded, with its impact potentially exceeding or at least matching that of the very strong El Nino episodes in 1997-1998 and 2015-2016. Mohd Hisham said the strong El Nino was also expected to occur alongside a positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), potentially intensifying the reduction in rainfall across the region.

items.title: Police arrest man suspected of setting 62-year-old Kepong lottery shop worker on fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Police have arrested a suspect in connection with the Aug 9 attack on an elderly woman who was doused with petrol and set alight at a lottery outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong. Sentul Police acting chief Supt Jasni Zolpa confirmed the arrest when contacted. “Yes, the suspect has been arrested and a press conference will be held today,” he said.

items.title: Former investment bank CEO among three to face MACC charges involving over RM136m
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Three individuals, including a former chief executive officer (CEO) of an investment bank, are expected to be charged under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act at the Sessions Courts in Kuala Lumpur and Seremban today. According to the court system, the former CEO will be charged before Sessions Court Judge Azura Alwi while a woman with the title Datuk, who is a company director, will be charged before Sessions Court Judge Suzana Hussin. The third individual, a chief financial officer (CFO) of a private higher education institution, is expected to face charges involving RM6.56 million in alleged corruption before Sessions Court Judge Kunasundary Marimuthu at the Seremban Sessions Court.

items.title: Syed Saddiq, Bella Astillah to wed on Oct 10 in all-white ceremony at Menara Merdeka Maybank (VIDEO)
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and his fiancée, singer-actress Bella Astillah, have reportedly announced that they will marry on October 10 at Level 118 of Menara Merdeka Maybank here. I do read it and take it seriously,” Syed Saddiq was quoted as saying. Syed Saddiq thanked the management of Menara Merdeka Maybank for allowing them to hold the solemnisation there, saying it would be among the first wedding ceremonies held on the building’s 118th floor.

items.title: UUCA explained: Malaysia’s 55-year-old campus control law and the repeal now on the table
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 19 — The Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) is set to be repealed, marking the end of a contentious 55-year legal era that defined, and often stifled, student activism in Malaysia. The road to restriction The UUCA was Malaysia’s answer to a wave of student unrest in the early-to-mid 1970s, when university students were among the country’s most vocal critics of poverty and inequality. The UUCA was tightened to curtail student activism following the Baling incident in December 1974.

items.title: Sarawak eyes direct Kuching–Jeju flights as AirBorneo expands regional tourism links
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 18 — Sarawak is seeking to establish direct AirBorneo Airways (AirBorneo) connectivity between Kuching and Jeju Island in South Korea as the state moves to expand access to key regional tourism markets. Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said South Korea was among the markets being considered for AirBorneo, with Jeju Island identified for the proposed direct connection. Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah said South Korea was among the markets being considered for AirBorneo, with Jeju Island identified for the proposed direct connection.

items.title: Kuala Pilah school lab roof collapse prompts chemical removal, JKR to assess safety
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 18 — The roof of a laboratory at Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Juasseh here suddenly collapsed at noon today. Kuala Pilah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Commander, Senior Fire Officer Mohd Idham Mohd Rodzi said no casualties were reported in the incident. — Bernama

items.title: 1MDB civil trial: Shahrol Azral denies Jho Low acted as PM, insists Najib briefed indirectly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Former 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) chief executive officer (CEO) Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi told the High Court today that he did not “treat” fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho, or Jho Low, as the country’s Prime Minister. Shahrol Azral: Yes. They named former prime minister Najib, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former general counsel Jasmine Loo Ai Swan, Vincent Beng, former chief financial officer Radhi Mohamad, Kelvin Tan, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds forecast in multiple states, MetMalaysia issues evening alert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across several areas in Peninsular Malaysia until 9pm today. In a statement, it said the affected areas include the whole of Perlis and several districts in Kedah, namely Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Pokok Sena, Padang Terap, Yan and Pendang. A similar warning has also been issued for several areas in Perak (Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Selama, Larut Matang and Kerian); Kelantan (Tanah Merah, Machang, Pasir Mas, Kota Bharu and Tumpat); Pahang (Maran, Rompin, Pekan and Kuantan); and Johor (Johor Bahru).

items.title: Court adjourns Pulau Batu Puteh appeal, Dr Mahathir’s lawyer seeks to add RCI report
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — The Court of Appeal here today adjourned the hearing of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad’s appeal after his lawyer indicated that he would file an application to adduce the Pulau Batu Puteh Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report as fresh evidence in the appeal. The three-member bench comprising Datuk Azizul Azmi Adnan, Datuk Ong Chee Kwan and Datuk Seri Mohd Radzi Harun allowed Dr Mahathir’s lawyer, Zainur Zakaria, two weeks to file the application. He said when the High Court judge decided on his client’s judicial review application, the RCI report was not available.

items.title: Sabah Fire Dept issues stern warning as eight areas hit by 12‑day dry spell
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 18 — Eight areas across seven districts in Sabah are experiencing a prolonged dry spell, with between 12 and 14 consecutive days without rain recorded as of yesterday. He said Keningau and Pitas recorded the longest dry spell, at 14 consecutive days, followed by the Wario Livestock Centre in Kota Belud and Ranau Station, at 13 days each. He added that four other locations — the Kimanis Agriculture Office in Papar, Laban Rata at Mount Kinabalu in Ranau, Serinsim Sub-Station in Kota Marudu and Kota Kinabalu Station — had recorded 12 consecutive days without rainfall.

items.title: High Court to deliver Aug 24 ruling on Negeri Sembilan Undang eviction summons
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 18 — The High Court today set Aug 24 for its decision on an originating summons filed by the Negeri Sembilan state government seeking an immediate eviction order for the official halls and residences of the Undang Rembau and Undang Sungei Ujong. The Negeri Sembilan state government filed separate originating summonses against Abdul Rahim and Mubarak on 16 and 17 July, respectively. Besides Abdul Rahim and Mubarak, other respondents named include occupants or individuals residing at the official halls and residences of Undang Rembau and Undang Sungei Ujong.
